newsitem.title: INDIA: India monsoon said "unsatisfactory" despite rain.
newsitem.headline: India monsoon said "unsatisfactory" despite rain.

text.p: A depression over the eastern Indian coast is likely to bring plentiful rains in some regions, but overall monsoon progress remains "unsatisfactory,", officials and crop analysts said on Wednesday.
A.V.R. Krishna Rao, a senior India Meteorological Department (IMD) official, told Reuters that a depression had formed over the Bay of Bengal sea and was likely to move in a northwest direction.

"Under its influence Orissa and Madhya Pradesh will get very good rains," Rao said. The central Madhya Pradesh state grows 80 percent of the country's soybean output and the eastern state of Orissa is mainly a rice growing region.
Rao said the western state of Gujarat and coastal areas of southern Andhra Pradesh state are also likely to get good rains under the influence of the depression.
IMD officials said 26 out of the 35 sub-divisions had so far received excess or normal rainfall.
"At least three more sub-divisions are expected to be covered under good rains this week," Rao said.
Analysts said that the progress of monsoon rains was not satisfactory and oilseeds and rice sowing has been affected to some extent.
"Monsoon rains are unsatisfactory," said a Bombay-based commodity analyst who asked not to be identified.
The analyst said that until July 23, 10 sub-divisions had received less than normal rains compared with only seven at the same time last year.
"This is the highest number (of deficient sub-divisions) since 1992," the analyst said. Rainfall had been very deficient mainly in oilseeds growing areas and some rice growing regions, he said.
"This is likely to affect the two crops although it is too early to quantify the adverse effect," the analyst said.
He said that the oilseeds sowing season was over and the targetted acreage under all the oilseeds could not be achieved due to deficient rains.
"Farmers are generally shifting to other crops which could be sown even with less rains," the analyst said.
Trade officials said rice sowing was completed in all the major rice producing regions but was affected in Andhra Pradesh, which contributes about five percent of the country's total rice output.
Government officials in the central city of Indore said nearly 95 percent of the targetted soybean acreage was covered under sowing after most central Indian belts received good rains.
"(Soybean) crop condition is very good due to favourable weather," said A.D. Majoomdar, a senior official of the state Agriculture Department.

Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said this week that the government was taking all steps to ensure adequate water availability if the monsoon withdrew earlier than scheduled under the impact of El Nino warm water currents. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
